_about: How names and recurring terms are written in this language. Every translation follows this file, so a name is always spelled the same way. Names are written by sound, never translated (the author's rule). The spellings here are first versions based on the written names: the author's own pronunciation is recorded in Legacy/Behind The Scenes/World Lore/Word Pronunciation/Unique Words Pronounciation.wav, so correct any spelling here and later translations will follow it. Add new names the first time they are translated.
rule: Story names in Thai script, by sound, with no spaces inside a single coined name (ทรังก์พีเพิล, แบล็กแซฟไฟร์) and a space between a person's given name and family or title parts (แฮร์รี ซันบี, จูลินา ฟอร์เวย์ ซักส์มายบอลส์). This covers coined world terms written as names too: creatures, plants, nari gels, spells, factions, guilds and ranks (Bleed Out = บลีดเอาต์, Red Winga = เรดวิงกา, Sapphire = แซฟไฟร์). A few descriptive place and object names whose plain meaning matters are translated (Nari Stones = หินนาริ, Black Honey = น้ำผึ้งดำ, Goodbye Cliff = «หน้าผาลาก่อน», Blood Book = คัมภีร์เลือด). The currency balls is บอล (บอลแซฟไฟร์, บอลเพิร์ล). Thai uses no full stops: sentences are separated by a space. The unit timehunk is ไทม์ฮังก์; A.G. and B.G. stay in Latin letters. Real people (Deovandski, Mitsukiven, Feiourm), the title and pets named in the afterwords (Peeta) stay in Latin letters. 'Sanbi shit!' (the Sanbi oath) is always วิญญาณเฒ่าแห่งซันบีเอ๊ย! ('Old Sanbi soul!'), the author's rule.
